name: Boreal-Sanctum

civilization.name: The Cryon Remnant
civilization.notes: Descendants of a once-spacefaring people driven underground by the Long Glaciation; they keep reactor-heated gardens alive beneath the ice and have not launched anything in four centuries.

description: From orbit Boreal-Sanctum is a white silence, its ice shell seamed with blue pressure ridges and pocked by frozen methane lakes that hold their gas like held breath. Aurora curtains hang over both magnetic poles at once—an anomaly no survey has explained—and beneath six kilometers of ice lies a warm black ocean the surface has never seen.

Nothing moves up there, and the wind makes the only sound: a thin whistle across the ridgelines that newcomers mistake for voices. Below, in cathedral caverns lit by reactor glow and farmed kelp-lamps, the air is wet and warm and smells of soil, and children grow up believing the sky is a legend.

The Cryon Remnant still maintains the orbital station their ancestors fled to when the Long Glaciation began, though no shuttle has climbed to it in four hundred years; it turns overhead like an unvisited grave. Deeper still, under the subterranean ocean's floor, seismic surveys keep returning the outline of something vast and deliberately buried—and on quiet nights, the Remnant's few remaining receivers catch a repeating signal whose source appears to be directly beneath it.

Salvagers covet the dark crystals harvested from the crystal caverns, worth fortunes for reasons the Remnant has never cared to learn, and would pay triple for directions to the buried thing. The Remnant's elders are dying faster than they can pass on the reactor rites; within a generation, either the gardens fail or someone finally opens what the ancestors sealed. The signal, patient as ice, waits for one or the other.
